question.question: Which of the following are recommended Docker practices when containerizing a machine learning model for production serving?

options.text: Use a multi-stage build to separate build dependencies from runtime dependencies
Install all Python packages with pip install --no-cache-dir to reduce image size
Run the container as root to ensure the model has access to all system resources
Pin base image digests (e.g., python@sha256:...) rather than using mutable tags like python:3.11
Copy the entire project directory including .git, __pycache__, and test files into the image

question.explanation: Multi-stage builds (a) keep final images small by discarding build tools. Using --no-cache-dir (b) prevents pip cache from bloating the image. Pinning digests (d) ensures reproducible, immutable base images. Running as root (c) is a security anti-pattern; containers should run as non-root users. Copying unnecessary files (e) increases image size and attack surface; use .dockerignore to exclude them.
